sentences.text: 1. This revision petition is filed by the petitioners being aggrieved by the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 09.06.2016 in C.C.No.885/2011 on the file of the II Additional Civil Judge and JMFC, Bhadravathi and its confirmation order dated 19.04.2017 passed in Crl.A No.5011/2016 on the file of the IV Additional District and Sessions Judge, Shimoga, Sitting at Bhadravathi, by which both the Courts have concurrently held that the petitioners herein are guilty for the offences punishable under Section 420 of Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC').

2. The ranks of the parties in the Trial Court will be considered henceforth for convenience Brief facts of the case:
3.

The case of the prosecution is that on 27.3.2009, accused Nos.1 and 3 said to have met PW.8 at Puri Jagannatha Temple and showed one duplicate diamond (replica of the so- called original) and asked him to purchase it by saying that the original is at Bhadravathi and it will be sold to him, if he had come to Bhadravathi.
Accordingly, PW.8 came to Bhadravathi along with his friend Susheel kumar and met accused Nos.1 and 3.
Both accused Nos.1 and 3 took them to the lodge and made them to stay there.
Further, PW.8 was told that he had to pay a sum of Rs.3,100/- to perform pooja to see nagamani.
PW.8 after negotiation gave Rs.2,100/- and asked them to perform pooja.
Accused Nos.1 and 3 took PW.8 and his friend on their bikes and showed an old temple which is situated on the bank of the canal.
There was a light which was being illuminated inside the temple and it was shown to P.W.8 and made him believe that it is a nagamani.
4. It is further averred in the complaint that P.W.8 was introduced to one old man and the said old man narrated the story as to how he possessed nagamani.
Further, the said old man offered him to purchase the said nagamani by paying Rs.25,00,000/-.
PW.8 expressed his inability and took time and went back to his native place.
5. It is further averred in the complaint that after sometime, P.W.8 contacted the accused and came back to Shivmogga as per the direction and stayed in a lodge.

According to the complainant, he paid a sum of Rs.4,50,000/- to accused Nos.1 and 3 and it is also stated in the complaint that at the time of giving money, it is said that the accused Nos.2, 4 and 5 were also present and all the persons were quarreling each other about their share and even after receiving the money, P.W.8 did not get the said nagamani and therefore, he went to Delhi and approached various authorities for having been cheated.
A complaint came to be registered by P.W.8.
Based on the complaint, the jurisdictional police have registered a case for the offence under Section 420 of IPC.
After conducting investigation, submitted the charge sheet for the above said offence.
6. To prove the case of the prosecution, the prosecution examined 8 witnesses as P.Ws.1 to 8 and got marked 4 documents as Exs.P1 to P4.
The Trial Court recorded the conviction against accused Nos.2 and 5 and acquitted the rest of the accused.
Being aggrieved by the same, accused Nos.2 and 5 approached the Appellate Court wherein the Appellate Court dismissed the appeal.
Hence this revision petition.

sentences.text:
Heard Shri Prasad B.S., learned counsel for petitioners and Shri Rahul Rai K., learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent - State.
8.

It is the submission of learned counsel for the petitioners that the findings of the Courts below in recording the conviction are against the evidence on record and therefore, the conviction is required to be set aside.
9. It is further submitted that the Trial Court recorded the conviction on the basis of assumptions and presumptions which is against the basic principles of law.
As per the evidence of PW.8, accused Nos.1 and 3 approached him and induced him to purchase nagamani and took Rs.4,50,000/- as advance.
The role of accused Nos.2 and 5 is not forthcoming in the evidence of PW.8.
In the absence of the evidence and overt acts against accused Nos.2 and 5, conviction ought not to have been recorded.

10. It is further submitted that merely because PW.8 being a resident of Maharajpura, Raibareli District, Uttar Pradesh, came and stayed at Bhadravathi and made certain allegations regarding the alleged transaction, that cannot be the ground to record the conviction.
However, the Trial Court and the Appellate Court misconceived the facts and the evidence on record and passed the impugned judgments which are required to be set aside.
Making such submission, learned counsel for petitioners prays to allow the petition.

11. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader vehemently justified the judgments of both Courts and submitted that the accused Nos.1 and 3 induced PW.8 to purchase the nagamani, which is considered a sacred diamond found in the hood of cobra and accordingly, received an advance of Rs.4,50,000/- with an intention to cheat PW.8.
Both the Courts have concurrently held that the petitioners are found guilty for the aforesaid offence.
Therefore, interference with the said findings is not necessary and hence, the revision petition deserves to be dismissed.

12. Having heard learned counsel for the respective parties and also perused the averments made in the judgments of the Courts below, it is relevant to refer to the essential ingredients of the offence under Section 420 of IPC, which read thus:-
"420. Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property.--Whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to make, alter or destroy the whole or any part of a valuable security, or anything which is signed or sealed, and which is capable of being converted into a valuable security
, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine."

On reading of the above said provision, it makes it clear that the accused must have dishonest intentions from the very beginning, which is sine qua non to hold the accused guilty for the commission of the said offence.

sentences.text: In the present case, as per the evidence of PW.8, on 27.03.2009, when he was coming out of Puri Jagannatha Temple, he said to have met accused No.1 - Raju and accused No.3 - Vijay.
Both have informed P.W.8 that they had some precious beads and stones and intended to sell those items.
As a sample, they showed one diamond like material and made him to believe that it is a precious diamond called as 'Golugumbada'.
When PW.8 told them that it was a duplicate, he was asked to come to Bhadravathi to see the original diamond.
14. Accordingly, P.W.8 and his friends along with accused Nos.1 and 3 came to Bhadravathi and stayed in the lodge situated at Bhadravathi.

P.W.8 said to have been introduced to the old man and the said old man narrated the story of having obtained the said nagamani and asked him to purchase the same by paying suitable sale consideration.
When P.W.8 expressed his inability to purchase the same, he was told to go back and come with money.

15. Further, the evidence of P.W.8 discloses that he came to Shivamogga as per the instructions of accused Nos.1 and 3 and stayed in the lodge situated at Shivamogga and said to have paid Rs.4,50,000/- to purchase nagamani.

According to P.W.8, there were other three persons who were present along with accused Nos.1 and 3 and they were quarreling with each other for their respective shares and they did not give the said nagamani to P.W.8.
Being aggrieved by the highhandedness of the accused, he had to go back to his native neither with his money nor with nagamani.
P.W.8 learnt that he has been cheated by the accused and thereafter, he approached various authorities and lodged a complaint.

16. The evidence of P.W.7 which discloses that he was working as PSI of the respective police station and he did not collect any evidence regarding the stay of P.W.8 either in Bhadravathi or in Shivamogga and also further discloses that he did not collect any document pertaining to the sources of fund out of which P.W.8 said to have paid to the accused.

17. Be that as it may, on conjoint reading of the evidence of all the witnesses, the findings of the Trial Court in recording the conviction against these accused are erroneous and not proper for the reason that the overt act against these accused about the offence stated supra has not been made out.
Further, it is noticed from the evidence that these accused have neither induced P.W.8, to deliver any goods or things for the purpose of cheating.
In fact, their presence in the alleged transaction has not been established by the prosecution, therefore, their conviction cannot be sustained.

Hence, I am of the considered opinion that these accused are liable to be acquitted for the offence stated supra.
18.

In the light of the observations made above, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
(i) The Criminal Revision Petition is allowed.

(ii) The judgment of conviction and order of Dharma vs State By Psi on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188055761/

- 10 - (iii) The petitioners / accused Nos.2 and 5 are acquitted for the offence under Section 420 of IPC.
